page.layout: One printed page, all in one column. Top: an ornamental border with no text. Then the title block, centred. Below it, the Hebrew verse in eight lines, with the marginal note "Psal. 1." in the left margin beside its first line. Then "Id est", the Latin verse with a large initial I, the signature lines, and the catchword at the lower right.
page.head: OCTASTICHON SYRIACUM
page.p: (Quadratis Hebræorum Characteribus propter Syriacorum defectum expressum.)
page.head: Præstantissimo ac Doctiss. D. Defendenti Sacrum.
page.l: רוחא דעמריא נך חכמא דמן מריא :
page.p: ILle beatus erit Sapiens, qui pectore versat Scripturam Domini, nocte diequè vacans Lectura: sic te dicemus jure beatum Quem ad Sophiam Dîam Spiritus intus agit: Est verbum Domini tua nocte diequè voluptas, Ut nobis hodiè hoc perspicuè patefit, Sicquè tuo exemplo referes illum Sapientem, Quapropter cunctis jure beatus eris.
page.notes: The large initial I of the Latin verse is joined to "Ille". The Hebrew lines are set in square Hebrew letters that are hard to read at this scan size; the transcription of the Hebrew may contain errors. The first Hebrew word has a large initial letter. The ornamental border at the top has no text.
